items.title: Kenya's marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir provisionally suspended over EPO test
items.why: The Athletics Integrity Unit has provisionally suspended Kenya's Peres Jepchirchir, the Olympic and world marathon champion. It says a sample taken in Kenya before her Sydney Marathon win in August tested positive for the banned blood booster EPO. A hearing will decide her case.

items.title: Israel closes Hebron and readies West Bank lockdown after soldiers killed
items.why: Two Palestinian gunmen attacked a checkpoint near Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday, killing two Israeli soldiers and wounding three, the Israeli army says; soldiers killed both gunmen. Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered Hebron closed and told the army to prepare a full West Bank lockdown.
items.matters: Netanyahu warned of a large military operation; Israelis vote in a national election on Tuesday, 27 October.

items.title: Gunman kills one and wounds four near Paris; terror inquiry opened
items.why: A man fired from a car at people in Trappes and nearby La Verrière, west of Paris, on Friday morning, killing one person and wounding four, including a child, police sources say. He was arrested in Coignières. Anti-terrorism prosecutors are investigating and examining a possible racist motive.
items.matters: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called it a terrorist attack; it comes a day before planned nationwide protests.

items.title: India's Jio Platforms share sale draws a record 10 million applications
items.why: Bidding closed on Friday for the first share sale by Jio Platforms, Mukesh Ambani's telecoms and digital firm. It is raising about $3.2bn, India's largest share sale in rupee terms. Exchange data showed more than 10 million applications, which Indian media report is a world first.
items.matters: The shares are due to start trading on 28 October, valuing the company at about $108bn.

items.title: Seoul mayor Oh Se-hoon cleared on appeal, keeping his job
items.why: The Seoul High Court on Friday overturned Oh Se-hoon's conviction for having a businessman pay for opinion polls before the 2021 mayoral by-election. The first trial had fined him 10 million won, enough to remove him from office. Judges said the key witness's testimony was unreliable.
items.matters: A final conviction would have ended his time as Seoul's mayor and barred him from public office for five years.

items.title: Japanese novelist Ryu Murakami dies at 74
items.why: The Japanese writer Ryu Murakami has died at home aged 74, Japanese news agencies reported on Friday. His family held a private funeral. His 1976 debut, 'Almost Transparent Blue', won Japan's top literary award, the Akutagawa Prize.
items.matters: His novels, including 'Coin Locker Babies', reached readers worldwide in translation.

items.title: Asian football backs Infantino for a fourth term as FIFA president
items.why: The Asian Football Confederation endorsed Gianni Infantino's bid for a fourth term as FIFA president at its congress in Tokyo on Friday. Two months ago the confederation had accused him of a 'fundamental breach of trust'. The election is in March 2027.
items.matters: Backing from 47 Asian football associations makes a challenge harder; UEFA says it will look for a rival candidate.

items.title: Asian shares fall again as the sell-off in tech stocks deepens
items.why: Tokyo's Nikkei fell 1.7% and Shanghai 1.8% in early Friday trading, AFP reports, and Seoul's Kospi was down about 2.4% by late morning, Yonhap reports. It follows a fall of about 2.6% in New York's tech-heavy Nasdaq on Thursday, when Meta's shares dropped nearly 7%.
items.matters: Doubts over whether heavy spending on AI will pay off are weighing on share prices around the world.

items.title: Japan's inflation rises above the central bank's 2% target
items.why: Japan's core consumer prices, which leave out fresh food, rose 2.1% in the year to September, up from 1.7% in August, official figures showed on 23 October. It is the first time in nine months the measure has been above the Bank of Japan's 2% target, Reuters reports.
items.matters: Many analysts now expect the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates again in December, Reuters says.

items.title: Venezuelans march for elections in first nationwide opposition protest in two years
items.why: Thousands marched in Caracas and other cities on Thursday at the call of María Corina Machado's Vente Venezuela movement, the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years. They want an election date; Machado says a vote must be held by July 2027. Her movement says police detained seven people.
items.matters: No election date has been set since US forces seized Nicolás Maduro in January; Delcy Rodríguez leads an interim government.

items.title: SK hynix drops plan to list its Solidigm unit in the US
items.why: South Korean chipmaker SK hynix said on 23 October it had halted plans for a US share listing of Solidigm, its storage-chip arm, citing market conditions. The listing had been expected to raise $10–15 billion. Korean regulators and shareholders had opposed it, Seoul Economic Daily reports.
items.matters: SK hynix is one of the world's biggest makers of the memory chips used in AI data centres.

items.title: Raye wins Mercury Prize for album This Music May Contain Hope
items.why: London singer-songwriter Raye won the Mercury Prize on 22 October for her second album, This Music May Contain Hope, at a ceremony in Newcastle, England. The prize, for the best British or Irish album of the year, carries £25,000; rivals included Olivia Dean and Paul McCartney.
items.matters: Judges called the album, which mixes jazz, soul and pop, 'the right choice' for its 'scale, structure, ambition and sheer charm'.

items.title: Europe's summer heat linked to over 50,000 deaths, scientists estimate
items.why: Researchers at Imperial College London and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine estimate that more than 50,000 people died early from heat in 854 European cities between June and August 2026, in two papers in Nature Health. Italy had the most, about 13,300.
items.matters: The authors attribute about two-thirds of the deaths to climate change, up from about 40% early this century.

items.title: Bournemouth beat 10-man AC Milan 3-0 in the Europa League
items.why: English club Bournemouth beat AC Milan 3-0 at home on 22 October after Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan was sent off in the 27th minute for shoving Tyler Adams. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier scored penalties and Amine Adli added a late free kick.
items.matters: In their first European season Bournemouth have won all three games, the first English club to do so since 1973, ESPN says.

items.title: US actor Tom Skerritt, of 'Alien' and 'Top Gun', dies at 93
items.why: The American actor Tom Skerritt has died aged 93 of natural causes, his family said on Thursday. He played Captain Dallas in 'Alien' and the instructor 'Viper' in 'Top Gun', and won an Emmy in 1993 for the TV drama 'Picket Fences'.

items.title: Monet's 'Iris' sells for €50m, a record for an auction in France
items.why: Claude Monet's late painting 'Iris', never before shown in public, sold for €50m including fees at Sotheby's in Paris on Thursday, the highest price for an artwork at auction in France. Sotheby's says the buyer is a private collector in Asia. The estimate was €22m–30m.
items.matters: The sale falls 100 years after Monet's death in 1926.

items.title: Gucci sales fall again as owner Kering's shares drop sharply
items.why: France's Kering said on Thursday that Gucci's sales fell 6% on a like-for-like basis to €1.29 billion from July to September, with few shoppers in mainland China. Group sales were flat at about €3.35 billion. Kering's shares then fell about 11%.
items.matters: Gucci brings in roughly half of Kering's profit, so its slide weighs on the group's turnaround plan.

items.title: Sri Lanka chase 430 to beat England despite Harry Brook's record 202
items.why: Harry Brook hit 202 off 116 balls, the fastest double century in one-day internationals, as England made 429 for four in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, on 22 October. Sri Lanka won by two wickets with one ball left, led by Pavan Rathnayake's 130.
items.matters: It is the second-highest successful chase in one-day internationals; England have lost both their tri-series games so far.

items.changed: Updated: Xinhua now reports 76 people injured
items.title: Magnitude 7.0 earthquake in northern Tibet kills at least 16
items.why: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Baqen county in Nagqu, northern Tibet, at 10:33pm local time on Thursday. Xinhua, citing local authorities, says at least 16 people died and 76 were injured; local officials say at least 339 homes collapsed.
items.matters: China's state broadcaster CCTV calls it the region's strongest earthquake in five years.

items.title: Study dates Van Gogh's The Starry Night to a July 1889 sky
items.why: South Korean researchers say the stars in Van Gogh's painting match the Hyades cluster, Venus and a thin crescent moon seen before dawn over Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France, around 22 July 1889, a month later than usually thought. The study is in Scientific Reports; some astronomers disagree.
items.matters: It shows how astronomy, old weather records and letters can help date famous works of art.

items.title: Man killed by crowd in Durban amid South Africa anti-migrant protests
items.why: Police say a crowd of about 50 people beat a foreign national to death on Thursday in central Durban, South Africa, on the sidelines of a march. His nationality has not been released and a murder case is open. Durban has seen months of protests against migrants.
items.matters: Soldiers were sent to Durban this month after rioting; Nigeria, Mozambique and Malawi say citizens have died in such attacks.

items.title: Malaria vaccine for children to cost about 40% less from 2027
items.why: UNICEF and the vaccine alliance Gavi have agreed to cut the price of the RTS,S malaria vaccine to €5.50 a dose. India's Bharat Biotech is taking over production from GSK. The lower price is due by early 2027 if a new factory gets WHO approval.
items.matters: The groups say the saving could pay for the full four-dose course for up to a million more children.

items.title: Young giant manta rays stay near Costa Rica's coast while adults roam
items.why: Researchers tracked giant manta rays off Costa Rica from 2018 to 2025 with acoustic and satellite tags. Young rays stayed in coastal waters, probably to avoid predators, while adults swam hundreds of kilometres, some as far as Guatemala. The study is in Frontiers in Fish Science.
items.matters: Adults lose protection when they leave coastal reserves, so researchers want neighbouring countries to protect migration routes together.

items.title: Hundreds flee clashes in Ethiopia's Moyale into neighbouring Kenya
items.why: Hundreds of people, mostly women and children, crossed into Kenya at the border town of Moyale after fighting between forces of Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regions, Kenyan police and officials said on Thursday. Reports link the clashes to a dispute over a regional flag.
items.matters: The Kenya Red Cross says it is giving shelter and food to 1,000 households while it counts those affected.

items.title: Ecuador detains opposition leader Luisa González in campaign-finance inquiry
items.why: Police in Ecuador detained Luisa González, the left-wing opposition leader who twice lost presidential races to Daniel Noboa, on Thursday. Prosecutors are investigating about $500,000 in alleged irregular funding of her 2023 campaign. She calls the accusations 'absurd'; her party calls it political persecution.
items.matters: It comes five weeks before local elections from which her Citizen Revolution movement has been suspended.

items.title: Investigators look for link between Nigeria and Kenya Ebola cases
items.why: Nigeria's health minister says its only Ebola patient is recovering and the case is contained; 46 contacts are barred from flying for 21 days. Kenya still has nine cases in one cluster. Africa CDC is checking whether the first patients in both countries met at Uganda's Entebbe airport.
items.matters: WHO's Africa director describes "a more complex outbreak landscape" now that three countries have cases.
items.changed: Updated: Nigeria says its patient is recovering and 46 contacts are barred from flying; no new cases

items.title: Personalised mRNA vaccine cuts melanoma return risk by 42% in large trial
items.why: Detailed results from a late-stage trial of 1,137 people whose melanoma had been removed by surgery show Moderna and Merck's personalised vaccine, given with the drug Keytruda, cut the risk of the cancer returning or death by 42% compared with Keytruda alone over about two years.
items.matters: Vaccines made for each patient's own tumour could become a new way to stop cancers coming back.

items.title: Nearly all the world's coral reefs face collapse by 2075, IUCN says
items.why: In its first global assessment of reef ecosystems, released on 22 October at the UN biodiversity summit in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, the International Union for Conservation of Nature rated 96% of shallow-water reef systems critically endangered. Heat stress from climate change is the main threat.
items.matters: Reefs support about a quarter of marine species; the IUCN says most are not yet lost and can still recover.

items.title: Turkey cuts its main interest rate to 36% as inflation slows
items.why: Turkey's central bank cut its main rate from 37% to 36% on 22 October, its first cut since January. Annual inflation fell to 29.7% in September, below 30% for the first time since 2021. The bank warned that high energy prices linked to the Iran war remain a risk.
items.matters: Borrowing gets slightly cheaper for Turkish households and firms; ING expects one more cut by the end of the year.

items.title: Australia's Snowy 2.0 hydro scheme could now cost A$25 billion
items.why: Snowy Hydro said on Thursday its pumped-hydro project in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales now has a target cost of A$22.2 billion, with up to A$25 billion allowed for. It was first priced at A$2 billion, and full operation has slipped to late 2029.
items.matters: The scheme is meant to store power for Australia's grid; ministers say abandoning it would raise electricity bills.

items.title: France bans protests in several cities after weekend riots and looting
items.why: French authorities have banned protests in several cities, including Lyon and Marseille on Saturday, after last weekend's looting and clashes. President Macron met student representatives on Friday. The interior minister says about 70,000 security personnel will be deployed for Saturday's marches.
items.matters: More than 2,700 people have been arrested since last Saturday, France's justice ministry says.
items.changed: Updated: Macron meets student groups; about 70,000 police and gendarmes to be deployed on Saturday

items.title: India chase 226 to beat New Zealand in first T20 in Christchurch
items.why: India beat New Zealand by four wickets with two balls to spare at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, New Zealand, chasing 226 after Glenn Phillips hit 82 not out. Sanju Samson made 67 from 33 balls, and India lead the five-match series 1-0.

items.title: International Criminal Court wins EU’s Sakharov human rights prize
items.why: The European Parliament awarded its 2026 Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought to the International Criminal Court on Thursday, its president, Roberta Metsola, announced in Strasbourg, France. The prize, worth €50,000, will be presented in December.
items.matters: It comes about two weeks after the Trump administration announced sanctions to cut the court off from US banks and companies.

items.title: France launches literary prize for fiction co-written with AI
items.why: Three French technology entrepreneurs have launched the Prix Pascal, which they call the first literary prize for unpublished French-language fiction written with artificial intelligence. Entrants must say which AI tools they used; entries close on 30 November and the winner, promised publication, is due in December.
items.matters: It follows weeks of dispute over suspected AI use by finalists for other literary prizes, including France's Prix Goncourt.

items.title: France reports first known human case of livestock virus Shamonda
items.why: French authorities say a severely immunocompromised patient treated in Lyon, who died in early October, had Shamonda virus. It is usually spread among cattle by biting midges and was not known to infect people. Officials think a midge bite in eastern France caused the infection.
items.matters: French health officials say there is no known risk to the general public.

items.title: Scientists send smells such as coffee and orange over the internet
items.why: Researchers at Ohio State University and China's Zhejiang Laboratory built 'Scentronic': an AI electronic nose recognises a smell and sends the data to a wearable device that recreates it from stored scented liquids. In tests, 14 volunteers named the five scents correctly about 73% of the time.
items.matters: It might one day let shoppers smell perfume or food online, though for now it copies only five smells.

items.title: Bone flute found at Troy, the dig's first musical instrument, minister says
items.why: A bone flute about 2,800 years old has been found at ancient Troy, in Türkiye's Çanakkale province, culture minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy said on 22 October. He says it is the first musical instrument found in over 160 years of digging there; a 4,500-year-old idol head was also unearthed.
items.matters: The dig's director links the flute to the 8th century BC, when Homer's epics are thought to have been written down.

items.title: Philippines raises interest rate more than expected as inflation hits 7.2%
items.why: The Philippine central bank raised its main rate by half a point to 5.5% on 22 October, its fourth rise this year; all 27 economists in a Reuters poll had expected a quarter point. Inflation reached 7.2% in September, pushed up by fuel and transport costs.
items.matters: The peso has lost nearly 10% since the Iran war began, making imports dearer, Reuters reports.

items.title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as it uses more AI
items.why: British bank Barclays said on 22 October it will cut about 5,000 jobs, around 5% of its staff, by the end of 2026, including 1,000 already gone. About 60% are in support roles, including software developers. Third-quarter pre-tax profit rose 12% to £2.3 billion, slightly below forecasts.
items.matters: Barclays says the cuts and wider use of AI should save it more than £1.1 billion.

items.title: Russian missiles and drones hit Kyiv hours after Putin agrees to talks
items.why: Russia struck Kyiv and 11 other Ukrainian regions overnight into Thursday, hours after agreeing to resume peace talks. Ukrainian officials say at least four people were killed and dozens injured, including children. President Zelensky says missiles with cluster warheads targeted the capital.
items.matters: Russia’s defence ministry says it downed 808 Ukrainian drones the same night, many heading for Moscow.

items.title: Australian court orders Apple to allow rival iPhone app stores
items.why: Australia's Federal Court ordered Apple on Thursday to let Australian iPhone users install apps from other app stores and websites, and to let developers use other payment systems, from March 2027. The case was brought by Epic Games, maker of Fortnite. Apple says it will appeal.
items.matters: The changes would affect an estimated 15 million Australian Apple users, ABC News reports.

items.changed: Updated: Estudiantes beat Flamengo to set up a final against Palmeiras
items.title: Palmeiras and Estudiantes to meet in the Copa Libertadores final
items.why: Argentina's Estudiantes beat Flamengo 3-2 on penalties in Rio de Janeiro on 22 October after both semi-final legs ended 0-0; goalkeeper Fernando Muslera saved three kicks. They will face Brazil's Palmeiras, who knocked out Fluminense on penalties a day earlier.
items.matters: The final is at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, Uruguay, on 28 November; Estudiantes have won the title four times.

items.title: Angel Reese leads Atlanta Dream to 2-1 lead in WNBA Finals
items.why: The Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 in Atlanta on Wednesday 21 October to lead the best-of-seven WNBA Finals 2-1. Angel Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds in a sold-out arena; the Valkyries made only 35% of their shots.
items.matters: Game 4 is in Atlanta on Saturday; the Dream are two wins from their first WNBA title.

items.title: Shark trapped in South Korean canal slips back in after third rescue
items.why: A 3-metre endangered dusky shark nicknamed Bukangi, stuck in a canal in the port city of Busan for a month, was guided out on 21 October but swam back in under a net that night. Officials are planning a new attempt; the shark has drawn over 1.6 million visitors.
items.matters: Officials worry that falling water temperatures and a lack of feeding put the shark's health at risk.

items.title: South Korea's central bank holds interest rate at 3% after two rises
items.why: The Bank of Korea kept its main interest rate at 3.00% on 22 October, a unanimous decision by its seven board members, after raising it in July and August. It said it wanted to watch how the earlier rises take effect; most analysts expect another rise in November.
items.matters: Booming chip exports are lifting South Korea's economy but adding to price pressures, Seoul Economic Daily reports.

items.title: Micron workers stage Taiwan's first chip-industry strike over AI profits
items.why: A union at chipmaker Micron's plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan, held a 24-hour strike on 22 October, which Nikkei Asia calls the first in Taiwan's chip industry. Only a handful took part and production was not halted, Caixin says. The union wants 15% of operating profit paid out as quarterly bonuses.
items.matters: Memory chipmakers are earning record profits from the AI boom, and workers want a bigger share.

items.changed: Updated: South Korea proposes military talks to the North on the border line and hotlines
items.title: North Korea to restart propaganda loudspeakers along the border with South Korea
items.why: Kim Yo Jong, sister of Kim Jong Un, says loudspeakers will be ready along the border within days. On Friday South Korea proposed military talks to agree the exact border line, restore military hotlines and prevent clashes. Seoul blames a North Korean mine for injuring three soldiers.
items.matters: North Korea did not answer a similar offer last year; Kim Yo Jong has dismissed Seoul's calls for dialogue.

items.title: Tesla's profit falls 43% as car sales revenue slips
items.why: Tesla said on 21 October that third-quarter revenue was flat at $28.05 billion, slightly above forecasts, but net profit fell 43% to $787 million, partly because of a paper loss on its SpaceX stake. Revenue from car sales fell 3%.
items.matters: Elon Musk said a planned Tesla-SpaceX chip factory could cost over $100 billion, Investing.com reports.

items.changed: Updated: Meta's shares fell nearly 7% on Thursday
items.title: Meta's shares fall 7% despite a 26% jump in sales
items.why: Meta, owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, said on 21 October that third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, but it expects 2026 capital spending of $135–145 billion, much of it on AI. Profit was cut by a $9.89 billion settlement charge. Its shares fell nearly 7% on Thursday.
items.matters: Spending on AI data centres turned Meta's free cash flow negative, at minus $2.1 billion for the quarter, Fortune reports.

items.changed: Updated: Dammam airport toll rises to two; Aramco tells staff to leave its headquarters
items.title: US orders non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
items.why: The US State Department on Wednesday ordered non-emergency staff and families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks. Saudi aviation officials say an attack on Dammam’s King Fahd airport that evening killed two people; drone debris near the Shaybah oilfield killed two more, the energy ministry says.
items.matters: Reuters and AFP report Saudi Aramco told staff to leave its Dhahran headquarters; the Houthis claim further strikes on Riyadh and Yanbu.

items.title: Typhoon Champi kills one in Taiwan and shuts schools and offices
items.why: Taiwan's emergency centre says one man died after waves swept him off a beach on Liuqiu island in Pingtung County, and at least 94 people were hurt. Schools, offices and the stock market closed on Friday, about 1,300 people were evacuated and nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled.
items.matters: The storm is forecast to brush north-eastern Taiwan, then head towards China's east coast and southern Japan.
items.changed: Updated: about 1,300 evacuated and nearly 1,000 flights cancelled

items.title: UAE nominates diplomat Lana Nusseibeh to be next UN secretary-general
items.why: The United Arab Emirates has nominated Lana Nusseibeh, its former UN ambassador, to succeed António Guterres, whose term ends on 31 December. No candidate has yet won Security Council backing, and a straw poll set for Friday was postponed, France 24 reports.
items.matters: If chosen, she would be the first woman to lead the United Nations.

items.title: Quebec publisher drops novelist Thélyson Orélien over AI use in prize-winning book
items.why: Publisher Boréal has cut ties with Haitian-born Quebec author Thélyson Orélien, saying an outside analysis found traces of AI in files of his debut novel, which won the Prix du roman Fnac and was withdrawn from the Goncourt list. Orélien denies using AI.
items.matters: Publishers and literary prizes are still working out how to handle books that may have been written with AI.

sources.name: The Canadian Press (via Yahoo News Canada)

items.title: US judge orders Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion over privacy
items.why: A judge in Santa Fe, New Mexico, ordered Meta on 21 October to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found in September that it misled residents about data privacy, counting 43 million violations. The state had sought at least $35 billion. Meta says it will appeal.
items.matters: Meta had asked for no more than $3.45 billion and calls the penalty 'a tax on speech'.

items.title: Physicists hold a single antimatter particle in a trap for months
items.why: A Northwestern University team in the US has trapped one positron, the antimatter twin of the electron, and controlled its quantum states, they report in Physical Review Letters on 21 October. The particle can be held for months; loading one takes 8 to 11 hours.
items.matters: A precise measurement could test whether matter and antimatter truly mirror each other, part of why the universe has matter.

items.changed: Updated: the flaws are now widely exploited; 32 UK government services offline
items.title: Hackers exploit critical PHP flaws as governments take websites offline
items.why: PHP, the language behind most websites, released emergency fixes on 21 October for two flaws that let attackers take control of servers. Amazon says they are now 'broadly exploited', and Cloudflare reports millions of attempts. In Britain, 32 government services went offline as a precaution, a minister says.
items.matters: Website owners must update PHP; the UK government says the outages are precautions and do not mean systems were hacked.

items.changed: Updated: latest Datafolha poll shows the two candidates level
items.title: Latest Brazil poll shows Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro tied before Sunday's run-off
items.why: A Datafolha poll released on Thursday puts President Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, level on 50% of valid votes each, with a two-point margin of error. A week earlier Bolsonaro led 51% to 49%. Brazilians vote on Sunday, 25 October.
items.matters: Polls underestimated Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round on 4 October, Bloomberg Línea notes, so the result is hard to call.

items.changed: Updated: Trump says Iran is making up the hits to raise oil prices; Brent near $113
items.title: Iran says it hit seven Gulf ships; Trump calls the claims fake
items.why: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards navy said on Thursday it struck four ships transferring oil in the northern Gulf and that three more hit mines west of the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump said Iran was ‘making up fake hits’ to push up oil prices. The claims are not independently confirmed.
items.matters: Brent crude rose about 4% on Thursday to around $113 a barrel, its highest since May, CBS reports.

items.changed: Updated: Putin agrees to resume three-way talks after 10 November and frees a US prisoner
items.title: Putin agrees to resume Ukraine peace talks after meeting Witkoff
items.why: Russia's President Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff for about three hours in St Petersburg on Wednesday. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia agreed in principle to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US after 10 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi. Russia freed US citizen Stephen Hubbard.
items.matters: Ushakov said Western and Ukrainian proposals offered 'little' of use; Zelensky says freezing the front line is the minimum.

items.changed: Updated: Brent rose above $114 on Friday
items.title: Oil rises above $114, its highest level since May
items.why: Brent crude rose 4% on Thursday to close at $113.17 a barrel, its highest close since 4 May, and traded above $114 on Friday. Traders point to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, risks to Gulf shipping and an outage at a Libyan oilfield.
items.matters: Oil prices feed into fuel, heating and shipping costs around the world.

items.changed: Updated: NYT reports US and Israeli plans for strikes after the midterms; ministers meet in Istanbul
items.title: Trump hints at further Iran strikes as ministers meet in Istanbul
items.why: The New York Times reports US and Israeli plans for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the 3 November midterms; Trump has not approved it. He says the US 'may do it a little bit further'. European and Middle Eastern ministers met in Istanbul on Friday.
items.matters: Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its terms are met, and reportedly warned it could hit Gulf airports and pipelines if attacked.

items.changed: Updated: Champi has weakened but has shut down most of Taiwan; one death reported
items.title: Typhoon Champi shuts down most of Taiwan as heavy rain begins
items.why: Champi was about 320 km east-southeast of Taiwan's southern tip on Friday, 23 October, with winds of 155 km/h, Taiwan's weather agency says. Schools, markets and flights were shut. Officials say one man died after being swept away by waves in Pingtung County and 94 people were hurt.
items.matters: Northern mountains could get 600–900 mm of rain by Saturday; the storm is then forecast to head towards southern Japan.

items.changed: Updated: El Salvador says gangs are holding the four; Bukele announces a rescue operation
items.title: El Salvador says Haiti gangs hold four of its air force members
items.why: President Nayib Bukele said on Wednesday that gangs are holding four Salvadoran aviation technicians missing since Sunday's ambush on the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force near Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince. He announced a military rescue operation and warned of a stronger response if they are not freed unharmed.
items.matters: Haiti's government calls their release an 'absolute priority'; no group has claimed the attack.
